blocks.text: Quick verdict

Oxylabs is the better choice for large-scale scraping, SERP and e-commerce data, where pool size, ZIP and ASN targeting and per-result scraper APIs matter. NodeMaven is the better choice for social media, multi-accounting and anti-detect browser users, where pre-screened IPs and long sticky sessions protect accounts, and it is cheaper at small volumes ($45 for 10 GB against $80 on Oxylabs pay-as-you-go) with rollover and cashback. At high volume, Oxylabs' $2.50/GB Corporate rate is close to NodeMaven's $2.20.

NodeMaven and Oxylabs both charge a premium over budget providers, but they are optimised for different jobs. Oxylabs is an enterprise network with a 175M+ residential pool, published 99.95% success rates and scraper APIs for large data pipelines. NodeMaven is a quality-first specialist whose IP Quality Filter screens each residential and mobile IP before assignment, aimed at account-based work. This comparison helps you decide which premium fits your use case.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven competes on IP quality rather than pool size. Every residential and mobile IP passes through its IP Quality Filter before it is assigned, with three strictness levels, and the company reports a 95% clean-IP rate. Proxyway's testing found the filter lowered fraud scores noticeably on sticky sessions. The pool is 30M+ residential plus 250K mobile IPs in 150+ countries, traffic rolls over, and you get up to 10% cashback on used gigabytes plus a guarantee that pays out for bad proxies.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
Oxylabs in 2026: what you get

Oxylabs is a Lithuanian web-data company and Bright Data's closest rival at the top of the market. It advertises a residential pool of more than 175 million IPs across 195 locations, publishes a 99.95% success rate for residential traffic, and sells seven product lines including datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies, a Web Scraper API and Web Unblocker. Onboarding is more sales-led than the mid-market providers, but self-service has expanded through 2026, including dedicated ISP proxies.

Strengths: One of the two largest residential pools available; Published 99.95% residential success rate; Strong scraper APIs that bill per result; Formal ethical-sourcing documentation for procurement. Weak spots: Expensive at low volume ($8/GB PAYG); Best rates need large monthly commitments; Residential trial goes through sales rather than self-service.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs Oxylabs

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

Oxylabs charges $8/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Monthly plans start with Starter at $30 for 5 GB ($6/GB) and a Basic tier around $100 for 20 GB, and the rate falls to $2.50/GB on the $2,500/month Corporate plan. Mobile traffic starts at $7.50/GB.

At 10 GB a month, NodeMaven is the cheaper option at about $45 against $80 for Oxylabs, roughly 44% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Oxylabs does not publish an exact price for that volume; NodeMaven comes to about $220. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while Oxylabs's does not (monthly plan allowances reset each cycle), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

By advertised size, Oxylabs (175M+) is about 5.8x larger than NodeMaven (30M+ residential + 250K mobile). Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and Oxylabs lists 195. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while Oxylabs offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and Oxylabs offers rotating and sticky sessions on residential and mobile. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its pool size and Web Scraper API suit large crawls. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling.

SERP and rank tracking: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its scraper API returns parsed search results. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need.

Social media and multi-account management: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. How Oxylabs compares: it works, but the pricing is built for volume, not a handful of accounts.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: city and ZIP targeting plus parsed e-commerce endpoints. How NodeMaven compares: fine for light checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: broad geo coverage with ASN targeting. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: good quality but a smaller pool.
Tight budgets: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG. How Oxylabs compares: entry pricing is among the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. Oxylabs: Residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. Oxylabs: Business verification on larger accounts. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and Oxylabs before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle NodeMaven vs Oxylabs faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; Oxylabs: residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 2, Oxylabs in 4, and 0 are ties. That makes Oxylabs the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while Oxylabs is strongest for large scraping pipelines with steady volume. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
